paper_metadata.title: Microstructural evolution and creep of Fe – Al – Ta alloys

evidence.quote: The microstructural evolution in Fe – Al – Ta alloys contain- ing 23 – 31 at.% Al and 1.5 – 2.2 at.% Ta has been studied in the temperature range 650 – 750 8C by annealing for 1, 10, 100 and 1 000 h.

evidence.section: 3.1. Evolution of the microstructure with temperature and time
evidence.quote: Figure 1 shows SEM micrographs of the alloy Fe-25.9Al-1.6Ta (all compositions in at.%) after annealing at 700 8C for various times. After annealing for 1 h (Fig. 1a) no changes in the microstructure were observed compared to the as-cast condition.

evidence.quote: After annealing for 10 h at 700 8C the microstructure still appears to be single phase in the SEM (Fig. 1b). However, TEM investigation of the sample showed that fringes are visible within the Fe – Al matrix (Fig. 2).

evidence.section: 3.1. Evolution of the microstructure with temperature and time

evidence.section: 3.1. Evolution of the microstructure with temperature and time

conflicts.description: The TTT diagram from the present data places the onset of C14 precipitation at lower temperatures and shorter times than reported by Risanti and Sauthoff.

evidence.section: 3.1. Evolution of the microstructure with temperature and time
evidence.quote: However, according to the present data, the precipitation of C14 starts earlier at lower temperatures than suggested in [16], e. g. at 650 8C at about 100 h instead at about 2 000 h.
